The statement is **true**. Here is the proof.

---

**Setup.** Let $K$ be a number field, $\mathcal{O}_K$ its ring of integers, $v$ a non-archimedean discrete valuation on $K$, and $\mathfrak{p}\subset\mathcal{O}_K$ the nonzero prime ideal corresponding to $v$. Let
$$\mathcal{O}_{K,v}=(\mathcal{O}_K)_{\mathfrak{p}}$$
be the localization of $\mathcal{O}_K$ at $\mathfrak{p}$; this is a DVR. Denote by $\widehat{\mathcal{O}_{K,v}}$ its completion with respect to the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic topology, and by
$$\varprojlim_n \mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n$$
the inverse limit of the natural quotient system.

We prove $\widehat{\mathcal{O}_{K,v}}\cong\varprojlim_n\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n$.

---

**Step 1. The completion of a DVR is the inverse limit of its truncations.**

The $\mathfrak{p}$-adic completion of $\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$ is, by definition/construction,
$$\widehat{\mathcal{O}_{K,v}}=\varprojlim_n \mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}.$$
This is the standard description of the completion of a local ring with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{p}\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$: the $\mathfrak{m}$-adic completion is the inverse limit of the quotients $\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{m}^n$, and $\mathfrak{m}^n=\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$.

---

**Step 2. Localization does not change the quotients: $\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n\cong\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$.**

Consider the natural map
$$\varphi_n:\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n\longrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v},\qquad a+\mathfrak{p}^n\mapsto a/1+\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}.$$

*Surjectivity.* Every element of $\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$ is of the form $a/s$ with $a\in\mathcal{O}_K$ and $s\in\mathcal{O}_K\setminus\mathfrak{p}$. Since $s\notin\mathfrak{p}$, the image $\bar{s}$ of $s$ in the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$ (whose maximal ideal is $\mathfrak{p}\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$) is a unit: $s\notin\mathfrak{p}\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$, so $\bar{s}$ lies outside the unique maximal ideal and is invertible. Hence $a/s\equiv a\cdot s^{-1}\pmod{\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}}$, and there exists $t\in\mathcal{O}_K$ with $st\equiv 1\pmod{\mathfrak{p}^n}$ (the inverse of $s$ mod $\mathfrak{p}^n$ can be lifted from $\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n$ since $s$ is a unit there). Therefore $a/s\equiv at\pmod{\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}}$, and $\varphi_n(at+\mathfrak{p}^n)=a/s+\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$. So $\varphi_n$ is surjective.

*Injectivity.* Suppose $a\in\mathcal{O}_K$ maps to $0$, i.e. $a/1\in\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$. Then $a/1=b/s$ for some $b\in\mathfrak{p}^n$, $s\in\mathcal{O}_K\setminus\mathfrak{p}$, meaning there exists $t\in\mathcal{O}_K\setminus\mathfrak{p}$ with $t(sa-b)=0$, i.e. $tsa=tb\in\mathfrak{p}^n$. Since $t,s\notin\mathfrak{p}$ and $\mathfrak{p}$ is prime (so $\mathfrak{p}^n$ is $\mathfrak{p}$-primary in the Dedekind domain $\mathcal{O}_K$), $ts\notin\mathfrak{p}$ implies $ts$ is a unit modulo $\mathfrak{p}^n$, hence $a\in\mathfrak{p}^n$. So $\ker\varphi_n=\mathfrak{p}^n/\mathfrak{p}^n=0$.

Thus $\varphi_n$ is an isomorphism for every $n\geq 1$.

---

**Step 3. The isomorphisms are compatible with the inverse systems.**

The maps $\varphi_n$ commute with the natural reduction maps $\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^{n+1}\to\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n$ and $\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^{n+1}\mathcal{O}_{K,v}\to\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}$, since both are induced by the identity on representatives. Therefore the $\{\varphi_n\}$ form an isomorphism of inverse systems, which induces an isomorphism on inverse limits:
$$\varprojlim_n\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n\;\cong\;\varprojlim_n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}.$$

---

**Step 4. Conclusion.**

Combining Steps 1 and 3:
$$\widehat{\mathcal{O}_{K,v}}=\varprojlim_n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}/\mathfrak{p}^n\mathcal{O}_{K,v}\cong\varprojlim_n\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n.$$

Hence the statement is **true**: the completion of the localization $\widehat{\mathcal{O}_{K,v}}$ is isomorphic to $\varprojlim_n\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n$. $\blacksquare$

---

**Remark.** The essential point is that localizing a Dedekind domain at a prime $\mathfrak{p}$ does not change any of the quotients $\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}^n$, because elements outside $\mathfrak{p}$ are already units modulo $\mathfrak{p}^n$. Thus the inverse limit — which sees only these quotients and their transition maps — is unchanged by localization, and equals the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic completion of the localized DVR.

### PROOF COMPLETE
